question: Identify the state abbreviations where, for both male and female legislators, the retention rate remains greater than zero at specific intervals of 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, and 10 years after their first term start date. A legislator is considered retained if they are serving on December 31 of the respective year. Only include states where both gender cohorts maintain non-zero retention rates at all six of these time points during the first decade of service.
sql:
WITH first_term AS (
    SELECT 
        id_bioguide,
        MIN(CAST(term_start AS DATE)) as first_term_start
    FROM legislators_terms
    WHERE term_start IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY id_bioguide
),
intervals AS (
    SELECT 0 as interval UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 4 UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 10
),
target_dates AS (
    SELECT 
        ft.id_bioguide,
        ft.first_term_start,
        i.interval,
        DATE_TRUNC('year', ft.first_term_start) + INTERVAL (i.interval) YEAR + INTERVAL '364 days' as check_date
    FROM first_term ft
    CROSS JOIN intervals i
),
all_legislators AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        lt.id_bioguide,
        l.gender,
        lt.state,
        td.check_date,
        td.interval
    FROM target_dates td
    JOIN legislators_terms lt ON td.id_bioguide = lt.id_bioguide
    JOIN legislators l ON td.id_bioguide = l.id_bioguide
    WHERE l.gender IN ('M', 'F')
      AND lt.state IS NOT NULL
),
retained AS (
    SELECT 
        al.gender,
        al.state,
        al.interval,
        COUNT(*) as retained_count
    FROM all_legislators al
    WHERE EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 
        FROM legislators_terms lt2
        WHERE lt2.id_bioguide = al.id_bioguide
          AND CAST(lt2.term_start AS DATE) <= al.check_date
          AND CAST(lt2.term_end AS DATE) >= al.check_date
    )
    GROUP BY al.gender, al.state, al.interval
),
total AS (
    SELECT gender, state, COUNT(*) as total_count
    FROM all_legislators
    GROUP BY gender, state
),
retention_rates AS (
    SELECT 
        r.state,
        r.gender,
        r.interval,
        100.0 * r.retained_count / t.total_count as retention_rate
    FROM retained r
    JOIN total t ON r.state = t.state AND r.gender = t.gender
)
